newsitem.title: JAPAN: China says needs aid, but respect for autonomy too.
newsitem.headline: China says needs aid, but respect for autonomy too.

text.p: China's central bank governor said on Monday that Asia-Pacific economic cooperation should respect countries' political differences and autonomy.

Speaking on the second day of the annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank in Fukuoka, southern Japan, Dai Xianglong said Asian nations, including China, need to strengthen economic cooperation to maintain growth.

But, he added: "Asia-Pacific economic cooperation should proceed under the precondition of respecting the political, economic and social differences among countries and people of this region and should be based on the principle of autonomy and willingness.
Dai told the board of governors of the 56-member bank, which provides soft loans to poor nations of the region, that China was still in need of help.
"As is well known, China is still a developing country, with a very low level of per capita income," he said.
"China needs concessional funds from the international community, particularly from such an official finance and development institution as the Asian Development Bank."
China was the ADB's top borrower in 1996, with $1.1 billion in loans.
